claim: The isolated DUOX1 PHD binds heme and has peroxidase activity
key_finding: Purified hDUOX1(1-593) and hDUOX2(1-599) contained no heme and showed no peroxidase or superoxide dismutase activity in any tested assay
context: human, recombinant extracellular domain, insect/mammalian expression
limitations: negative in vitro result; cannot exclude activity needing an unidentified partner or cofactor

claim: The PHD retains a usable heme site
key_finding: Isolated hDUOX1/hDUOX2 PHDs titrate heme with only low micromolar affinity, carry no heme after purification and have no peroxidase activity; authors invoke an unobserved conformational change
limitations: micromolar binding is weak and non-specific for a b-type heme protein; no structure of the heme-loaded state

claim: The PHD contacts the NOX module and DUOXA1 in the assembled complex
key_finding: Cryo-EM of the human DUOX1-DUOXA1 2:2 complex (PDB 7D3E high-calcium, 7D3F low-calcium) places the PHD on top of the transmembrane module in contact with DUOXA1
limitations: two conformers of one human complex; no PHD-deleted structure

claim: Heme-ligand and catalytic positions of animal peroxidases are substituted in DUOX1
key_finding: Sequence-anchored superposition of the DUOX1 PHD on goat lactoperoxidase (2R5L): 325 CA pairs, RMSD 1.23 A; all seven mapped catalytic/heme positions substituted in hDUOX1 (Q222->Y104, D225->L107, H226->S108, E375->R241, R465->Q328, H468->T332, N554->C423)
context: human DUOX1 chain A residues 22-619 of PDB 7D3F vs PDB 2R5L
limitations: 30.2% identity; the E375 column sits in a poorly aligned loop (see E9)

claim: Catalytic loss is a human or primate peculiarity
key_finding: Across 140 vertebrate DUOX1/DUOX2 orthologs the proximal His column is Thr in 98%, the ester-Asp column is Leu in 99%, the prox-side Arg column is Gln in 90%; none carry the lactoperoxidase residue at those three columns
context: 140 UniProt vertebrate DUOX1 (n=22) and DUOX2 (n=118) sequences
limitations: DUOX2-skewed sample; pairwise alignment to human DUOX1, no profile HMM

claim: The ancestral heme site is an empty pocket in DUOX1
key_finding: Free volume at the superposed heme site is 292 A3 in DUOX1 vs 494 A3 in heme-stripped lactoperoxidase; 22 DUOX1 atoms fall within 2.5 A of the modelled heme, Glu327 OE1 1.6 A from the modelled Fe; 29 lining residues have median RSA 0.04
limitations: single conformer; a hypothetical heme-loaded state could rearrange side chains

claim: Conserved PHD surface is enriched at inter-subunit interfaces
key_finding: Among 255 PHD surface residues (RSA>0.20), interface residues have median 93.3% ortholog identity vs 58.2% elsewhere (Mann-Whitney p=2.9e-06, Cliff's delta +0.36; Fisher OR 3.31 for >=90% identity, p=2.9e-05). Per partner: TM/NOX cis +0.288 (p=4.5e-03), DUOXA1 cis +0.322 (p=7.5e-03), DUOXA1 trans +0.312 (p=2.2e-03); DUOX1-DUOX1 PHD protomer interface -0.161 (p=0.54). Contact sets replicate between 7D3F and 7D3E, Jaccard 0.93-0.97
context: PDB 7D3F chain A vs chains B, C, D; conservation from 140 orthologs
limitations: conservation and burial are correlated; two conformers of one complex

claim: The PHD caps or channels the ROS produced by the NOX module
key_finding: The PHD occludes only 6.6 of 37.4 A2 of the outer heme b; the TM module alone gives the same 37.4 A2. Nearest PHD residue to the outer heme Fe is Leu602 at 10.9 A and no free-volume channel reaches it. Over the same structure the PHD buries 1522 A2 of NOX-module and 1042 A2 of cis DUOXA1 surface
limitations: one conformational state; a transient open channel is not excluded

claim: All heme-ester positions are unambiguously lost
key_finding: The column aligned to lactoperoxidase E375 carries Glu in 65% of orthologs (88/118 DUOX2, 2/22 DUOX1) but in a different local motif (bird GNEN-P vs mammal GNRE-P vs LPO ASEQ-I); human DUOX1 has Arg241 with Glu242 adjacent. This loop aligns poorly and the column assignment there is low confidence
limitations: a single ambiguous column; no covalent heme is detectable in isolated PHDs (E1, E2)

claim: The invertebrate DUOX PHD is catalytically active and uses a covalent heme
key_finding: C. elegans BLI-3 peroxidase domain forms a covalent heme link through Glu238; my alignment places BLI-3 Glu238, Arg327 and His330 at exactly the lactoperoxidase E375, R465 and H468 columns, which validates the column transfer
limitations: invertebrate; does not constrain the vertebrate enzyme directly

claim: Human DUOX1 is involved in cuticle development
key_finding: Ce-Duox1 RNAi gives a blistered cuticle from loss of tyrosine cross-linking; GO:0042335 is annotated involved_in on human Q9NRD9 with ECO:0000315 from this paper
confidence: high for the worm, none for human
limitations: organism carry-over onto a human entry; humans have no cuticle

claim: The PHD controls whether DUOX releases O2.- or H2O2
key_finding: The determinants of H2O2 vs superoxide release in DUOX/NOX map to the transmembrane A-loop region, not the extracellular PHD
limitations: indirect for the PHD; shows where the determinant is, not what the PHD does

claim: DUOXA1 is required for DUOX1 maturation and surface delivery
key_finding: DUOXA1 is required for ER exit, maturation and functional cell-surface expression of DUOX1
limitations: does not localise the requirement to the PHD

claim: Downstream peroxidase chemistry needs the DUOX PHD
key_finding: The DUOX/SCN-/lactoperoxidase system of airway surface liquid uses a separate secreted heme peroxidase (LPO) to convert DUOX-derived H2O2 into hypothiocyanite
limitations: pathway-level; assigns the peroxidase step to LPO, not DUOX1
